M2M Connectivity · Sales & Marketing

Faster campaigns.
Better-qualified conversations.

A six-month AI campaign pilot — two initiatives, judged on pipeline, not content volume.

James Richmond · Marketing Director · November 2026

The problem

Good opportunities wait too long for marketing

  • Campaign setup takes 4–6 weeks from a sales brief
  • Too much depends on hand-offs and one person's time
  • Our engineers' expertise rarely reaches customers at scale
  • We can't reliably trace which campaigns produce real opportunities

What that costs sales

Fewer opportunities pursued, slower response to market needs, and enquiries we can't qualify or attribute.

Initiative 1

Sales opportunity → campaign in ~5 working days

1 · BriefSales gives a short brief: problem, offer, evidence, outcome
2 · StrategyAI drafts positioning and messaging from M2M's own knowledge; you comment
3 · PackLanding page, emails, social and creative produced together
4 · Launch & trackCampaign ID in Zoho; qualified enquiries go to a named owner

For sales

  • Bring an opportunity, get a campaign within a week
  • Named target accounts and a follow-up plan

Quality controls

  • Every claim traces to an approved source
  • You see every campaign before it goes live
Initiative 2

One recording → a full campaign

A planned 20–30 minute sales + engineer conversation on a target product area. AI turns it into a ready-to-run campaign.

1 · PlanSegment, product, offer and 5–7 real customer questions
2 · RecordSales asks; engineer answers with real deployments
3 · ExtractAI finds key moments, messages, proof points, objections
4 · ApproveEngineer checks claims (~15 min)
5 · Produce & optimiseScheduled, tracked, best assets pushed harder

What one video produces

Hero cut · 6–10 short clips · landing page with chapters · offer (site assessment, demo trial, "talk to the engineer") · 3–4 email sequence · article + one-page PDF · ad variants · rep-ready clips for prospects · FAQ entries for web and search

How they fit

Reactive speed + planned depth, one system

Initiative 1 — reactive

Sales spots an opportunity; marketing responds fast with a complete campaign.

Initiative 2 — planned

We choose a product area and build a campaign around our engineers' expertise.

Both use the same approved knowledge base, the same campaign pack format and the same Zoho tracking. Our differentiation is specialist expertise applied to customer problems — this gets it in front of customers faster.

How we'll judge it

Success means pipeline, not posts

  • Sales-accepted opportunities and pipeline from each campaign
  • Enquiry → opportunity conversion and cost per opportunity
  • Campaign ready ≤5 working days from a complete brief
  • ≥80% of assets accepted without major rewrites

Decision at month 6

Expand, adjust or stop each initiative on its own results. If it isn't helping sales, we stop it.

Six months

The pilot plan

Month 1Agree opportunity definition; baseline; pick 2 opportunities + 1 recording topic
Month 2Build intake, knowledge base and review
Month 3Prototype both; compare with manual work
Month 4Launch first campaign from each
Month 5Repeat, improve weakest step
Month 6Review results and decide
The ask

What we need from sales

First two weeks

  • Agree what counts as a qualified opportunity
  • Two real opportunities with a short brief each
  • One salesperson (and an engineer) for a 30-min recording

During the pilot

  • A named follow-up owner per campaign; 48h response
  • Campaign ID recorded in Zoho
  • Top customer questions to shape recordings
  • 30 minutes a month to review results

Next step: 30 minutes this week or next to pick the first two opportunities and the recording topic.
